scope: Shared-reading policy change and inspected-data regression
policy: Positive coaching counts as reading. Explicit negated instructions remain blocked unless authored context. Both voices use normal alignment and one-shot history.
changed_expectations: Positive quoted prompts now count. In shared coaching-only and child coaching-before cases, the adult actually says the full anchor, so target emission is desired; this is not literal-omission evidence.

fresh_shared.note: An adult coaching the whole anchor now counts, including hibernate. Such a composite contains the word and is not a literal-omission control. Existing forward jumps can skip earlier checkpoints.

unrelated.note: Six policies replay each of four fresh unrelated ASR timelines; these are four audio trials, not 24.

saved_challenges.close_word_counter_basis: Historical strict-literal comparison. All five listed emissions are subsequently user-accepted under pod policy; see post_evaluation_pronunciation_review.

limits: All samples are inspected regressions; no held-out or natural-family accuracy claim.
Shared inputs are the same constructed audio as the previous frozen test; only goals implied by the user-approved policy change.

Existing overlap, long-pause recognition, missing-word, and close wrong-word limitations are not repaired by this policy. The five reviewed close-word emissions were subsequently accepted by the user for the pod; retain the literal-word comparison separately.
Whole-sentence parent reading can use existing forward-jump rules and skip earlier checkpoints. No speaker identity is inferred.
Positive-coaching policy does not fix the separate Singapore prefix-confirmation miss.
Negation remains a bounded text veto on effects/assistance; it is not a new hold-progress state.
One coached hibernate phrase appears in ASR but remains unconfirmed; accepting coaching does not guarantee every phrase triggers.

Known close-word false emissions remain. Existing missing finish effects and interruption losses remain. The five reviewed close-word emissions were subsequently accepted by the user for the pod; retain the literal-word comparison separately.
No new human listening labels, population accuracy or verified word latency are claimed.
